newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb says earnings fall after charges.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb says earnings fall after charges.

text.p: Health products company Bausch & Lomb said Wednesday its earnings fell in the third quarter, and cited charges for the sale of its Oral Care Division and for a settlement of a class action suit over its contact lens marketing.

The company, well known for its contact lens care and other vision products, said its earnings fell by two-thirds to $14.4 million, or 25 cents per share, from $43.5 million, or 75 cents per share, a year ago.
The results in the latest quarter included a charge of $10 million after taxes in connection with the proposed settlement of the class action lawsuit announced Aug. 1.

The suit charged that Bausch & Lomb had sold identical contact lenses under different trade names and at different prices. Lawyers representing consumers in the suit said the company agreed to provide $34 million in cash and $34 million in products under the settlement.
The latest quarter's earnings also included $6.3 million in losses associated with the sale of the company's Oral Care Division in mid-September.
Excluding the charges, earnings were down 28 percent to $30.7 million, or 54 cents per share, from a year ago.
Net sales rose slightly to $477.2 million from $476.8 million, the company said.
It said worldwide sales of contact lens care products declined 2 percent due to lower revenues from rigid gas permeable lens care solutions.

Contact lens sales were up 19 percent as sales of its disposable and planned replacement contact lenses grew sharply. Prescription pharmaceutical sales gained 14 percent and Miracle-Ear hearing aids rose 8 percent.
The stock of Rochester, N.Y.-based Bausch & Lomb was off 75 cents to $35.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
